To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed image decomposition methodology allows a full-field comparison of the experimental and numerical results, which is not possible using the conventional strain field comparison methods.

the image decomposition method allows for an objective comparison between experimental and numerical results, and it was found that the hyperplastic material model with a constant bulk modulus and a strain hardening behavior is the most suitable for the material studied.

1) the image decomposition methodology is a valid tool to perform a direct comparison of experimental and numerical results in the field of quasistatic numerical/experimental indentation analysis in soft materials; 2) the image decomposition method is a powerful technique for the analysis of full field data independently of their orientation or scale; 3) the image decomposition technique is a useful tool for the validation of numerical results obtained from the quasistatic analysis of the indentation in soft materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
validating numerical analyses in soft materials using a full field experimental approach.
the application of a novel approach for validation of numerical simulations using full-field data, and its use in a quasistatic numerical/experimental analysis in soft materials.
a validation approach for the quasistatic numerical analysis of indentation in soft materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for this specific problem, the hyperplastic model is a good choice for simulating the mechanical behavior of the material.
the numerical analysis performed using the Ogden hyperplastic model is the most accurate one.
both material models provide a good level of approximation for the experimental results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed approach can be used for validating numerical simulations of soft materials, such as rubbers, and it can be extended to other materials and other loading situations, such as cyclic loading.
the numerical analysis of indentation tests in soft materials using a hyperplastic material model can be validated with the help of 3D Digital image Correlation.

the numerical model that best fits the experimental results is the one that considers the effect of the strain softening on the material behavior, which is the one that is closer to the real material behavior.

the Image Decomposition methodology can be used to validate numerical models with experiments in the case of indentation tests in soft materials.
the proposed image decomposition approach is a powerful tool to validate the numerical analysis of quasistatic experiments in soft materials.
the Image Decomposition methodology can be used as a validation tool for numerical models in soft materials.
